articles.title: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen
articles.summary: Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’ • This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
body: Joshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.

Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised star Sacha Baron Cohen early in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.

The movie involves Loudermilk being recruited by another Cohen character, the ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, to help form a citizens’ warrior force to protect US borders, making use of his top-secret new weapon: a gun disguised as buttocks.

Along with fellow recruit Michael Aboud, the chair of the El Paso county Republican party, Loudermilk joins Morad on a mission to stop the birth on US soil of the baby of a fictional South American drugs kinpin. This involves abducting a woman apparently in labour, abandoning her in a deserted medical facility, kidnapping her newborn child (a lifelike prosthetic) and driving it in a zipped bag to the border in order to deliver it by drone to Mexico.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Grok Releases First AI-Generated ‘Odyssey’ Episode, Months After Promising ‘Historically Accurate’ Full-Length Film
articles.summary: Months after Elon Musk promised that his AI tool Grok Imagine would create an entirely AI-generated, feature-length version of “The Odyssey,” the tech mogul has partially followed through on the claim.
body: “Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer,” he wrote, together with an AI-generated 3-minute short of “The Odyssey” posted by an X user.

At the time, “Doctor Strange” and “The Black Phone” director Scott Derrickson pulled no punches and addressed Musk directly on social media to call out the absurdity of the project. “Clearly @elonmusk doesn’t know shit about cinema & he stopped reading in his 20s,” Derrickson wrote on Musk’s social media platform, X. “His opinions on art are worthless.”

While no further statement accompanied the AI-generated episode — or Musk’s original tweet about creating a “historically accurate” version of “The Odyssey” — the move comes after the tech trillionaire repeatedly criticized the film ahead of its release, especially the casting of Elliot Page as Achilles’ Ghost and Lupita Nyong’o as Helen of Troy.

Musk claimed that Nolan cast both actors to satisfy the Academy’s representation and inclusion standards for Oscar eligibility; in March, he wrote that “Chris Nolan is an anti-White racist,” saying he cast Nyong’o only because “He wants the awards.”

articles.title: DJ Pikachu: Pokémon Goes EDM With Lasers, Battles and Marshmello in 30th Anniversary Concert at Intuit Dome
articles.summary: Gotta rave ’em all! Pokémon celebrated its 30th anniversary with an epic EDM concert at LA’s Intuit Dome with DJs Marshmello and Alison Wonderland on Saturday night. Billed as Pokémon Night Out, the show mixed together the creatures from the popular video games and trading cards with the lasers…
body: After launching 30 years ago and growing into a worldwide phenomenon across entertainment, gaming and merchandise, Pokémon ended its banner year in style with Marshmello and Alison Wonderland, two fans of the brand themselves. And LA’s high-tech Intuit Dome was the perfect venue for the one-of-a-kind show.

Marshmello then took the stage and appeared as if his DJ booth was floating in the center of the video wall as Pokémon-themed visuals swirled all around him. Smoothly animated Pokémon that looked like they were ripped straight from the latest games flew, danced and battled right next to the DJ as he performed. The masked DJ played to both fans of his own EDM style and Pokémon gamers with eye-popping lasers that criss-crossed through Intuit Dome and fan-favorite Pokémon that appeared in short vignettes on screen.

articles.title: Jessica Biel Says ‘7th Heaven’ Reboot Will ‘Modernize’ the Show Now That TV Has ‘Less Limitations’: ‘We Were Very Careful About What Our Audience Wanted’
articles.summary: Nearly 20 years since the conclusion of “7th Heaven,” and over a year since the news broke about its reboot, original star Jessica Biel is giving fans an update on the new iteration of the show, including how she plans to “modernize” it for today’s audience and what she hopes to accomplish on set as
body: As a producer, Biel plans to create a “safe place for people to be really creative and really vulnerable,” she explained.

“When I’m on set as a producer, I’m always thinking about the safety net of the set and the communication that you hope you can have — free-flowing communication with your actors and your crew,” she added. “You just want to create a safe place for people to be really creative and really vulnerable, because a lot of the stuff that I’m doing now, the content that I’m doing now, it’s emotional stuff. It’s people really putting themselves out there on the chopping block emotionally, and if you don’t have that space protected, I think it’s hard. It’s hard to give those kinds of performances.”

Variety exclusively broke the news of the “7th Heaven” reboot back in May 2025. At the time, sources said that the new iteration of the show would focus on a diverse family, and that none of the original cast members would appear.

articles.title: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ Scores $19.5 Million in Huge Second Weekend, ‘Clayface’ Leads With $24 Million Debut
articles.summary: Just when you thought you’d seen everything… A three-hour documentary (in its second weekend of release) has earned almost as much as a new comic-book adaptation at the domestic box office. Although Warner Bros. and DC’s R-rated “Clayface” was comfortably at No.
body: “Opening ‘You Can See Everything’ in 855 theaters was a really smart move, allowing the film to establish itself and build momentum before going much wider,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “The fact that we’re seeing a documentary deliver such a significant second-weekend increase is remarkable.”

“Clayface” opened alongside a smattering of new releases, including Laika’s stop-motion animated “Wildwood,” Black Bear’s offbeat romantic comedy “Wicker” and Sony’s literary adaptation “Klara and the Sun,” starring Jenna Ortega.

“Wildwood” debuted at No. 3 with $11.2 million from 2,718 venues, launching above projections of $6 million to $8 million. It’s a promising start for original animation, which has been challenged in the years following the pandemic. And “Wildwood” has the benefit of sterling reviews (a rare 100% on Rotten Tomatoes) and audience scores (an “A” grade on CinemaScore exit polls), which should help the film stick around beyond its opening weekend. However, this movie carries a hefty $100 million price tag (stop-motion animation is labor-intensive and takes years to produce) and likely won’t turn a theatrical profit.

articles.summary: The horror short by Swedish director David F. Sandberg went viral 10 years ago thanks to a Reddit post that New Line turned into a blockbuster.
body: Warner Bros. released Lights Out on July 22, 2016, and it grossed $148 million globally on a $4 million budget. With a sequel still in the works, Sandberg, who later helmed Shazam!, offers this advice to young filmmakers: “Keep creating because you never know what’s going to resonate. We didn’t know that Lights Out was going to work.”

articles.title: Star Trek's DeForest Kelley Was In A '50s Western Starring 2 Movie Legends That's Worth Watching
articles.summary: DeForest Kelley, who originated the role of Dr. "Bones" McCoy on Star Trek, had a key role in a classic 1950s Western alongside two absolute titans of cinema.
body: In 1957, future "Star Trek" actor DeForest Kelley played the minor role of Morgan Earp in John Sturges' Western classic "Gunfight at the O.K. Corral." It was a star-studded affair, with Burt Lancaster playing Wyatt Earp and Kirk Douglas playing Doc Holliday. It's very much worth watching. If you keep your eyes peeled, you might also recognize a young Dennis Hopper as Billy Clanton and Lee Van Cleef as a character named Ed Bailey.

Prior to his stint playing Dr. McCoy on "Star Trek" in 1966, Kelley was a well-established and quite prolific Western performer. One of his very first TV roles was in an episode of "The Lone Ranger," and one can find many, many oaters across his résumé. He was on "Gunsmoke," "Dick Powell's Zane Grey Theater," "The Adventures of Jim Bowie," "Boots and Saddles," "Have Gun — Will Travel," "Rawhide," "Bonanza," "The Virginian," and a heaping fistful more. His Western output was far greater than the sci-fi he made.

articles.title: ‘Clayface’ Rolls to $24M Box Office Opening as ‘You Can See Everything’ Shines in Second Weekend
articles.summary: A24's documentary about Elizabeth Holmes grossed 25 percent more in its sophomore frame than its first, while Laika's 'Wildwood' took third place.
body: Clayface made its mark in its opening weekend at the box office as the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything continued to build on its momentum with an impressive sophomore frame.

Warner Bros. released director James Watkins’ body-horror feature Clayface in more than 3,400 North American theaters, and it grossed around $24 million domestically for the weekend. While just under the studio’s initial projection of $25 million to $30 million, this represents a solid result for the genre offering from DC Studios that carries a modest $44 million budget. It added $19 million from 76 international markets.

Audiences and critics alike found Clayface worth smiling about, as it earned an A- CinemaScore while holding a 75 score from reviewers on Rotten Tomatoes and a 94 from audiences. In his r e view for The Hollywood Reporter, critic Frank Scheck called Clayface “a big swing that definitely pays off.” Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie star in the story of Matt Hagen (Harries), an actor who turns to a scientist (Ackie) for assistance when his face becomes disfigured.
points: A24's documentary about Elizabeth Holmes grossed 25 percent more in its sophomore frame than its first, while Laika's 'Wildwood' took third place.

articles.title: Ben Affleck Starred In A Short-Lived TV Series Based On An Incredibly Popular Book
articles.summary: This best-selling book sparked a movie adaptation and a beloved TV show, but did you know it also inspired a short-lived TV show starring Ben Affleck?
body: In 1990, author H.G. Bissinger published a popular nonfiction book that detailed the story of the Periman High School football team, the Tigers, through their 1988 season. It was called "Friday Night Lights: A Town, a Team, and a Dream," and it was terrifically popular, becoming a #1 New York Times Bestseller, a fact the publishers happily included on the cover of the 25th anniversary edition.

Many may not know this next part, but in 1993, TV creators Michael Pavone and Dave Alan Johnson loosely adapted "Friday Night Lights" into a little-seen and very short-lived NBC drama called "Against the Grain," which starred a young Ben Affleck, four years before "Good Will Hunting" and long before he started making his best work behind the camera.

I say "loosely adapted" because a lot of the details were changed for the TV series, with pretty much only the Texan high school setting and football coaching motifs retained. However, this show wasn't one of Affleck's bigger successes.

articles.title: Sam Fender calls out ticket prices ahead of tour
articles.summary: The Geordie singer appears to have lowered ticket prices ahead of his upcoming tour.
body: Sam Fender has said he has removed a ticket category from sale after being unhappy with pricing for his upcoming tour.
The 32-year-old announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour earlier this week, which will visit Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Manchester in summer 2027.
While tickets are yet to go on sale, Fender responded to a post on social media which claimed to outline the expected ticket prices.
The Geordie musician now appears to have lowered the prices and said the "costs are astronomical compared to two years ago" but he could not control the venue or ticketing fees.
points: The Geordie singer appears to have lowered ticket prices ahead of his upcoming tour.

articles.title: How Star Trek Hater Robert Picardo Became An Icon Of The Franchise [Exclusive]
articles.summary: Robert Picardo, who has played the no-nonsense Doctor across multiple Star Trek series, tells us about his evolution from hater to veteran of the franchise.
body: "Star Trek" may be for everyone, prioritizing diversity and strength in different perspectives and a prevailing sense of unity no matter our differences, but it's not necessarily for everyone, if you know what I mean. From a certain point of view, a franchise filled with goofy-looking aliens and nerdy sci-fi concepts and characters with a penchant for breaking into Shakespeare is bound to keep some viewers at a distance. That, of course, applies equally to actors... even some who've gone on to become "Star Trek" royalty in their own right.

"Voyager" star Robert Picardo's healthy sense of skepticism regarding the series that brought him into the property's limelight is the stuff of legend. In fact, it perfectly matches that of the character he played, the fastidious and typically ill-tempered Doctor. Although he's mellowed out quite a bit in the years since his debut, most recently during his return in "Starfleet Academy," few figures in "Trek" can rival The Doctor in terms of simply not wanting to be bothered by all the zaniness surrounding him. As it turns out, Picardo shared that exact same reluctance when he was first cast in the role.
points: Robert Picardo, who has played the no-nonsense Doctor across multiple Star Trek series, tells us about his evolution from hater to veteran of the franchise.

articles.title: Former ’60 Minutes’ Executive Producer Bill Owens Joins Creator Media Company Newpress
articles.summary: Owens will be EP of the new firm, which raised money from Emerson Collective and media veterans Jesse Angelo, David Leavy, Brent Montgomery and Patrick Steel.
body: Former CBS 60 Minutes executive producer Bill Owens is getting into the creator economy.
The veteran journalist is joining the media startup Newpress as its EP.

Newpress was founded by Johnny and Iz Harris, who are both established YouTube filmmakers (the company includes Johnny Harris’ current YouTube channel). The company is planning to launch a handful of new shows over the next few months, with a longer-term goal of having 12-16 channels led by creators who are subject matter experts.
Owens will work with all of the creators to develop new shows and bolster their production. It is his first role since exiting 60 Minutes last year.
